ModifyHpLostAfterOsty.issue: The formula is exact: `target != base.Owner -> amount`, `amount < 1m -> amount`, else `1m` (SlipperyPower.cs:19-30) vs powers.py:1520-1522. The BeforeOsty/AfterOsty phase collapse is already resolved as faithful by damage_pipeline (Osty redirection is waived, so its steps 8 and 11 fold into one call). What is left is that the sim runs ALL seven HP-loss modifiers in one registration-order chain where C# runs a BeforeOsty pass then an AfterOsty pass then an AfterOstyLate pass -- hook_dispatch gap G3, not re-verdicted. It matters for THIS power because HardenedShellPower is the only `ModifyHpLostBeforeOsty*` implementer in the game and must therefore run before this one, and min-then-cap is not cap-then-min; see audit/records/power/hardened_shell.json, where the ordering was EXECUTED and found to coincide today (sim order ['HardenedShellPower', 'TheBoot', 'TungstenRod']). DORMANT by that executed check. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterDamageReceived.maps_to: sts2_rl/powers.py:1615-1624 `SlipperyPower.on_damage_received` (dispatched from sts2_rl/cmds.py:185-186 behind the killing-blow guard, via sts2_rl/hooks.py:677-690)
AfterDamageReceived.rationale: The entry's sole complaint -- 'which number is tested', hp_lost vs a supposedly pre-HP-loss-modifier UnblockedDamage -- rests on a misreading of the game. CreatureCmd.cs:266-271 applies BeforeOsty then AfterOsty ModifyHpLost and only then calls LoseHpInternal, and Creature.cs:453 sets `UnblockedDamage = currentHp - CurrentHp`, so SlipperyPower.cs:34's `result.UnblockedDamage >= 1` tests the same post-modifier number the sim's powers.py:1623 tests (hp_lost, cmds.py:166/186). With HardenedShell's cap on the same creature both sides see the same value -- 0 when the shell is spent (no decrement on either side), 1 otherwise (decrement on both) -- so the named 'Slippery lasts longer in the sim' outcome cannot arise. Cap side is unchanged and already faithful (powers.py:1611-1613 vs SlipperyPower.cs:25-29).  RECONCILED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): this entry was recorded `gap` against pre-campaign code and the divergence is closed today. The issue it replaced read: Right slot (AfterDamageReceived -> cmds.py:122, killing-blow guard on both sides) and the right condition in shape: `target == base.Owner && result.UnblockedDamage >= 1` vs `target is self.owner and amount >= 1`. The divergence is WHICH NUMBER is tested. C#'s `UnblockedDamage` is post-block but PRE-HP-loss-modifier, so the stack is consumed whenever any damage got through the block. The sim's `amount` is `hp_lost`, i.e. post-block AND post-`modify_hp_lost` (cmds.py:86 then :122) -- and this power's own cap is one of those modifiers. It still reaches 1, so a stack is consumed either way HERE; but with HardenedShellPower's cap (or a future 0-flooring modifier) on the same creature the sim can see 0 where C# sees a positive UnblockedDamage and so FAIL to consume a stack, making Slippery last longer in the sim. Same `hp_lost`-for-`UnblockedDamage` substitution as power/hardened_shell.json's AfterDamageReceived entry -- one mechanism, one verdict (rule 3). DORMANT: no ported creature carries both Slippery and a second HP-loss modifier. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
